subject: Science
question_text: Two identical bulbs A and B are connected in series with a 6V battery. How does the current through Bulb A compare to the current through Bulb B?
student_answer: Bulb A has more current than Bulb B
student_explanation: Bulb A is closer to the positive terminal, so it uses up some current before the rest reaches Bulb B.
expected_answer: The current is exactly the same through both bulbs because in a series circuit there is only one continuous path for charge flow.
observed_error: Attenuation / consumption mental model of electric current

subject: Science
question_text: A wire is connected from the battery positive terminal to a light bulb, but the return wire to the negative terminal is disconnected. Will the bulb light up?
student_answer: Yes, it will light up briefly
student_explanation: Electricity flows from the battery into the bulb. It doesn't need to return to produce light.
expected_answer: No, because electric charges require a continuous, unbroken closed conducting loop to flow.

subject: Science
question_text: If a 12V potential difference is applied across a 4 ohm resistor, what is the current?
student_explanation: I multiplied 12 by 4 using the formula V*R.

subject: Science
question_text: When a second resistor is added in parallel to an existing circuit, what happens to the total equivalent resistance?
student_explanation: Adding more resistors always adds more resistance because you have more obstacles.
expected_answer: Total resistance decreases because adding parallel branches creates additional paths for current flow.
observed_error: Additive resistance bias failing to understand reciprocal conductance
